x: The most notable club performer was Charlie Walker who, in finishing seventh in 52m.42s., seems to be returning to his very best form. Our team achieved quite a creditable fifth position which was only six points behind that of the second team.

Charlie Walker was soon in the first bunch which was headed by Hugh Foord of Brighton and when seen again at the end of the first lap had established himself in second place some distance behimd Foord.
This year's race,held on a cold damp day, ran true to form with Charlie Walker, who always performs so well over our own courses, the winner by the comfortable margin of 47 seconds.
Toward the end of the first of the three laps Eric Gebbett was our first scorer way back in 49th place followed closely by Charlie Walker 55th.

The first of the National Relays was staged in April 1951 over the Mitcham to Brighton course, and we were the winners from Thames Valley H. by nearly three minutes. Our team ran in this order:- C.W.

The odd thing is, that Bill Lucas is still the last man to take the individual title (1946): but he has only held this distinction by the skin of his teeth for, since then, a Belgravian has finished runner-up on no less than six occasions---the unlucky fellows being:- C.W.

C.W.Walker, the winner of our recent road race for Novices, did well in his first “open” race to finish in 34th position, but we missed the services of Arthur Bruce, who could not get leave from his unit.
